sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The resolution was passed at the **Lahore Session** of the Muslim League (March 1940) presided over by **Muhammad Ali Jinnah**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: It rejected the **Federal Scheme** of the Government of India Act 1935, arguing it was totally unsuited to Indian conditions.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: It proposed that geographically contiguous units should be demarcated into regions where Muslims were numerically in a majority, such as the North-Western and Eastern zones, to be constituted as **Independent States**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The term 'Pakistan' was not explicitly used in the text of the resolution; it was coined by **Choudhry Rahmat Ali** in 1933.

items.definition: The official document drafted by the Working Committee of the AIML, emphasizing that no constitutional plan would be acceptable to Muslims unless designed with their consent.
The belief that Hindus and Muslims are two distinct nations with different social orders, religions, and cultures, making a unified democratic state impossible.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: Consolidation of Muslim political identity under the banner of the Muslim League.
• **Key Application 2**: Strategic leverage against the Indian National Congress during the Quit India Movement and subsequent negotiations.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Ambiguity regarding the number of states (singular vs plural) and the status of princely states.
• **Solutions**: Eventual transition to the Mountbatten Plan (1947) which finalized the partition boundaries.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'L-A-M-P' (Lahore, AIML, March, Pakistan-demand).
• **Decoded Meaning**: L (Lahore Session), A (AIML), M (March 1940), P (Pakistan Resolution).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often asks if the word 'Pakistan' was in the original 1940 resolution. It was NOT. The resolution used the term 'Independent States'.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Communal Veto' to describe how the League used the resolution to block constitutional progress until their demands were met.

keyTakeaways: The resolution marked the point of no return for the partition of India.
It explicitly rejected the 1935 Act's federal structure.
The resolution was a strategic political tool to consolidate Muslim support under Jinnah's leadership.
